column1: # AQL Language Specification: Argument Usurping (usurp / /u)
# Format: input<TAB>expected<TAB>description
# usurp f         → wrap a function so its signature arg order is reversed
# name/u          → same, as a word-suffix modifier (resolves + usurps name)
# name/ur         → usurp combined with ref: leave the wrapper as inert data
# quote (usurp f) → capture the usurped wrapper as inert data
# A usurped fn called `usurped a b c` dispatches the original as `f c b a`.
# Like ref/`/r`, the wrapper is an unquoted Function value: it dispatches
# when args follow (forward / paren-grouped) and stays inert under quote or
# when reffed.
def sub2 fn [[a:Integer b:Integer][Integer][a sub b]]  sub2 10 3
column3: baseline: sub computes a-b

column1: def sub2 fn [[a:Integer b:Integer][Integer][a sub b]]  usurp (ref sub2) 10 3
column3: usurp reverses args: now 3-10

column1: def sub2 fn [[a:Integer b:Integer][Integer][a sub b]]  sub2/u 10 3
column3: /u modifier reverses the same way

column1: def sub2 fn [[a:Integer b:Integer][Integer][a sub b]]  (usurp (ref sub2)) 10 3
column3: paren-grouped reffed wrapper dispatches

column1: def inc fn [[n:Integer][Integer][n add 1]]  inc/u 5
column3: usurp of a 1-arg fn is a no-op on order

column1: def cat3 fn [[a:String b:String c:String][String][a add b add c]]  cat3/u 'x' 'y' 'z'
column3: usurp reverses all three args

column1: def f fn [[a:Integer b:String][String][b add (a convert String)]]  f 7 'hi'
column3: baseline: heterogeneous sig

column1: def f fn [[a:Integer b:String][String][b add (a convert String)]]  f/u 'hi' 7
column3: usurped sig is [String Integer]; a=7 b='hi'

column1: def sub2 fn [[a:Integer b:Integer][Integer][a sub b]]  def ops {rev: (usurp (ref sub2))}  ops.rev 10 3
column3: wrapper captured in a map dispatches via dot-access

column1: def inc fn [[n:Integer][Integer][n add 1]]  quote (usurp (ref inc))
column3: quoted usurp is inert data — the Function value itself

column1: nope/u
column3: /u on an unbound name

column1: def x 5  x/u
column3: /u on a non-fn binding is rejected

column1: def x 5  usurp x
column3: usurp word rejects a non-function value (Function slot unmatched)

column1: # ─── /ur : usurp combined with ref — leave the reversed wrapper INERT ───
# /ur (and the equivalent /ru) build the reversed-arg wrapper but, like
# /r, leave it on the stack as data without invoking. The held wrapper
# dispatches when re-stepped (grouped in a paren, or via apply).
def sub2 fn [[a:Integer b:Integer][Integer][a sub b]]  sub2/ur
column3: /ur holds the reversed wrapper (params b,a) — not invoked

column1: def sub2 fn [[a:Integer b:Integer][Integer][a sub b]]  sub2/ru
column3: /ru is the same as /ur (order-independent modifier letters)

column1: def sub2 fn [[a:Integer b:Integer][Integer][a sub b]]  (sub2/ur) 10 3
column3: grouped reffed-usurp wrapper dispatches (reversed: 3 sub 10)

column1: def sub2 fn [[a:Integer b:Integer][Integer][a sub b]]  (sub2/ru) 10 3
column3: /ru grouped dispatches identically

column1: def sub2 fn [[a:Integer b:Integer][Integer][a sub b]]  10 3 sub2/ur apply
column3: apply a held reversed wrapper (reversed args → 10 sub 3)

column1: def f ([a:Integer b:Integer] => [a sub b])  (f/ur) 10 3
column3: reffed-usurp of an anonymous fn, grouped → reversed dispatch

column1: # ─── cond-first `if` via usurp (the motivating use case) ───
# Plain `cond if then else` mis-binds because the stack `cond` falls into
# the trailing `else` slot. Reversing if's args with /u (or usurp+ref)
# makes the branches read else-first with the condition LAST.
if true [99] [88]
column3: baseline: if cond then else

column1: if/u [88] [99] true
column3: if/u reverses: if/u else then cond — true → then (99)

column1: if/u [99] [88] false
column3: false → else (99) under reversed order

column1: usurp (ref if) [88] [99] true
column3: inline usurp+ref of if, reversed order, cond last

column1: # ─── usurp must receive a function VALUE — group ref/r, don't pass bare ───
# `usurp` is forward-eligible on a Function slot, so its argument must
# already BE a Function value when collected. A bare `f/r` ref-word token
# is not yet resolved at collection time — group it in parens.
def sub2 fn [[a:Integer b:Integer][Integer][a sub b]]  usurp (sub2/r) 10 3
column3: usurp of a grouped /r reference works

column1: def sub2 fn [[a:Integer b:Integer][Integer][a sub b]]  usurp sub2/r 10 3
column3: bare `usurp f/r` — the ref-word isn't resolved as a forward arg; group it

column1: def sub2 fn [[a:Integer b:Integer][Integer][a sub b]]  usurp sub2
column3: bare `usurp f` — usurp takes a Function value, not a word name

column1: # ─── KNOWN LIMITATION: a usurp wrapper bound by name and then called as
#     a word currently fails the fn return check (0 values). Use the
#     inline / paren / map-slot / `/u` forms above instead. This row pins
#     the current behavior; lift it (and this note) when the named-bind
#     dispatch path is fixed.
def sub2 fn [[a:Integer b:Integer][Integer][a sub b]]  def fu (usurp (ref sub2))  fu 10 3
column3: named-bound usurp wrapper called as a word — known limitation
